subject: Environment
sub_topic: Environmental Impact Assessment — process and stages

concepts.name: Legal Basis of EIA: EIA Notification 2006 vs. EIA Notification 1994
key_dimensions: Parent legislation: Environment Protection Act 1986, Section 3 — rule-making power vs. EIA as a standalone notification
Key shifts from 1994 to 2006: decentralization to State-level appraisal, introduction of Category A and B projects
Mandatory vs. voluntary EIA era: pre-1994 vs. post-1994 landscape
UPSC trap: EIA is a subordinate legislation (notification), NOT an Act — frequently confused

concepts.name: Project Categorization: Category A vs. Category B (B1 and B2)
key_dimensions: Criteria for categorization: scale, location (Ecologically Sensitive Areas), and potential impact thresholds
Appraisal authority distinction: Category A → MoEFCC + Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC); Category B → State EAC (SEAC) + State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA)
Category B2 projects: exempted from EIA but require Environmental Permission — a major UPSC trap
Recent controversy: EIA Draft 2020 proposals to expand B2 (exemption) category — civil society objections

concepts.name: Screening Stage: Entry Point of EIA Process
key_dimensions: Definition: determination of whether a project requires EIA and under which category it falls
Role of the project proponent vs. regulatory authority in initiating screening
Exemptions at screening stage: projects below threshold limits automatically classified as B2
UPSC trap: Screening is NOT a public participation stage — confusion with Scoping and Public Hearing

concepts.name: Scoping Stage: Terms of Reference (ToR) Determination
key_dimensions: Purpose: defining the boundaries, parameters, and depth of the EIA study
Who issues ToR: EAC/SEAC issues standardized ToR within 60 days; if not issued, proponent can proceed with standard ToR
Baseline data collection period: minimum one season data (excluding monsoon) — a frequently tested specific detail
UPSC trap: Scoping is mandatory for Category A and B1 but the public is NOT formally involved at this stage under 2006 notification

concepts.name: Environmental Impact Assessment Report (EIA Report/EIS): Structure and Content
key_dimensions: Mandatory components: project description, baseline environmental status, impact prediction, Environment Management Plan (EMP), risk assessment
Role of accredited consultants: only MoEFCC-accredited EIA consultants can prepare the report — Quality Council of India (QCI) accreditation link
Executive Summary requirement: must be available in local language for public hearing
UPSC trap: EIA Report ≠ Environmental Clearance; it is an INPUT to the appraisal process, not the final decision

concepts.name: Public Consultation Stage: Public Hearing Mechanism
key_dimensions: Nodal agency: State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) or Union Territory Pollution Control Committee (UTPCC) conducts public hearing — NOT MoEFCC directly
Timeline: public hearing must be conducted within 45 days of receipt of request from SPCB
Notice requirement: 30-day prior notice in two national and two local newspapers + District Collector notification
Projects EXEMPTED from public hearing: strategic/defence projects, modernization of irrigation projects below threshold, projects in CRZ, pipeline projects — high UPSC trap area

concepts.name: Exemptions from Public Consultation: Categories and Controversies
key_dimensions: Listed exemptions under EIA 2006: expansion projects with <50% capacity increase, pipeline/transmission lines, ropeways, small hydropower (<25 MW) in certain cases
Industrial Estates/Export Processing Zones: public hearing at estate level, not individual unit level — a trap
EIA Draft 2020 proposal: expanding exemption list to include solar parks, highways — major environmental governance controversy
Judicial scrutiny: NGT rulings on whether exemptions violate the 'precautionary principle' (Rio Declaration Principle 15)

concepts.name: Appraisal Stage: Role of Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC)
key_dimensions: Composition of EAC: sectoral experts, environmental scientists — chaired by independent expert, NOT a government secretary
Appraisal outcomes: Environmental Clearance (EC) granted / EC with conditions / rejected / returned for more information
Validity of EC: 5 years for construction phase (10 years for River Valley projects) — specific timelines are UPSC favourites
UPSC trap: EAC is an ADVISORY body — final EC is granted by MoEFCC (for A) or SEIAA (for B), NOT by EAC itself

concepts.name: Environmental Clearance (EC): Grant, Conditions, and Post-clearance Monitoring
key_dimensions: Specific conditions in EC: environmental safeguards, green belt development, corporate environment responsibility (CER) — distinguished from CSR
Post-EC compliance monitoring: Half-Yearly Compliance Reports (HYCR) submitted to MoEFCC and Regional Offices — public disclosure mandate
Deemed EC controversy: if authority does not respond within prescribed time, it does NOT constitute deemed approval (unlike some other regulatory regimes)
UPSC trap: EC is project-specific AND site-specific — transfer of EC to another party requires fresh application

concepts.name: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA): Concept and India's Gap
key_dimensions: Definition: SEA applies EIA principles to policies, plans, and programmes (PPPs) — upstream of project-level EIA
India's status: SEA is NOT legally mandated in India unlike EU (SEA Directive 2001) — a significant governance gap
Examples where SEA would apply: National Highway development plans, coal block allocation policies, river interlinking programme
UPSC relevance: frequently asked as 'what is missing in India's EIA framework' — SEA is the standard answer

concepts.name: Cumulative Impact Assessment (CIA): Concept vs. Indian Practice
key_dimensions: Definition: assessing combined impacts of multiple projects in a region/basin — e.g., multiple hydropower projects on a single river
Indian case study: Supreme Court order on Alaknanda/Bhagirathi basin — MoEFCC commissioned CIA for Ganga tributaries after Uttarakhand disaster 2013
Gap in EIA 2006: CIA is not a mandatory stage — projects assessed individually, ignoring synergistic impacts
UPSC trap: CIA ≠ Cumulative EIA Report; CIA is a broader planning tool while individual project EIA can include cumulative impact chapter

concepts.name: EIA Draft Notification 2020: Key Proposed Changes and Controversies
key_dimensions: Post-facto clearance (Clause 26): allowing regularization of projects that commenced without EC — criticized as legitimizing violations
Reduced public consultation period: from 30 days to 20 days for public response
Expansion of strategic/defence exemption and B2 category — reducing transparency
Current status: Draft 2020 was NOT finalized as of knowledge cutoff — EIA 2006 remains operative; UPSC may ask about specific provisions proposed

concepts.name: National Green Tribunal (NGT) and EIA: Appellate Jurisdiction
key_dimensions: NGT Act 2010, Section 16: any person aggrieved by an EC order can appeal to NGT within 30 days
NGT vs. High Courts: NGT has exclusive jurisdiction over EIA appeals — High Court writ jurisdiction can be contested (UPSC trap on concurrent jurisdiction)
Landmark NGT orders on EIA: Vedanta Alumina case (public hearing validity), Mopa Airport case (scope of reconsideration)
Locus standi at NGT: broader than courts — any 'aggrieved person' can approach, not just directly affected parties

concepts.name: Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notification and EIA Interface
key_dimensions: CRZ projects require SEPARATE CRZ clearance in ADDITION to or instead of standard EIA EC — a critical UPSC trap on which authority grants which clearance
CRZ 2019 vs. CRZ 2011: key changes — No Development Zone reduction, tourism flexibility, island development
Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM): SEA-like approach for coastal areas — World Bank supported project in India
Overlap: projects in CRZ that are also Category A require both CRZ + EIA clearance from MoEFCC (dual clearance trap)

concepts.name: Ecologically Sensitive Areas (ESA)/Ecologically Sensitive Zones (ESZ) and EIA Categorization
key_dimensions: ESZ notification under EP Act 1986: buffer zone around Protected Areas — projects within ESZ automatically escalated to Category A regardless of size
Supreme Court ruling (T.N. Godavarman case): mandatory 10 km ESZ around all National Parks/Wildlife Sanctuaries as interim measure
EIA trap: a project BELOW Category A threshold becomes Category A if located in ESZ/CRZ/interstate boundary area
Forest Clearance under Forest Conservation Act 1980: separate from EC but often required simultaneously — two-window clearance system

concepts.name: Environment Management Plan (EMP): Mitigation and Monitoring Framework
key_dimensions: EMP components: mitigation measures, monitoring plan, institutional arrangements, budget allocation, timeline — must be part of EIA report
Corporate Environment Responsibility (CER): 2% of project cost for local area development — distinct from CSR (Companies Act) and a UPSC favourite confusion point
Green Belt/Compensatory Afforestation requirements: specified in EMP, monitored through HYCR
UPSC trap: EMP is prepared by the project PROPONENT (not the regulator) and forms a legally binding schedule of the EC conditions

concepts.name: Accreditation of EIA Consultants: QCI-NABET System
key_dimensions: NABET: National Accreditation Board for Education and Training under Quality Council of India (QCI) — accredits EIA consultancy organizations
Mandatory accreditation: since 2010, only NABET-accredited firms can prepare EIA reports for Category A and B1 projects
Conflict of interest issue: project proponent HIRES and PAYS the EIA consultant — structural bias in the system
UPSC trap: QCI is not a statutory body — it is a non-profit set up by Government of India and industry associations (CII, FICCI, ASSOCHAM)

concepts.name: Prior Environmental Clearance (PEC) vs. Prior Forest Clearance (PFC): Sequential vs. Concurrent Processing
key_dimensions: Historical issue: EC required FC to be obtained first, causing delays — now concurrent processing allowed under green single-window reforms
Parivesh Portal: single-window clearance system integrating EC, FC, CRZ, and Wildlife clearances — launched 2018
In-principle approval vs. final approval: Stage I FC (in-principle) can be obtained concurrently with EC; Stage II FC only after EC grant
UPSC trap: Parivesh does NOT eliminate separate clearances — it only creates a common application portal; each clearance remains legally independent

concepts.name: Violation and Penalty Mechanism in EIA: Enforcement Gap
key_dimensions: EP Act 1986 penalties: imprisonment up to 5 years and/or fine up to ₹1 lakh (extendable by ₹5,000/day for continuing violations)
Post-facto clearance debate: EIA 2006 does NOT allow post-facto EC — Supreme Court ruling in Alembic Pharmaceuticals vs. Rohit Prajapati (2020) reaffirmed this
Monitoring agencies: Regional Offices of MoEFCC + SPCBs — but chronic under-staffing limits enforcement effectiveness
UPSC trap: NGT can impose penalties and direct closure independently of criminal proceedings under EP Act — concurrent remedies available

concepts.name: Environmental Appraisal of River Valley and Hydropower Projects: Special Provisions
key_dimensions: All river valley projects ≥50 MW or ≥10,000 ha submergence are Category A — regardless of state boundary
Extended EC validity: 10 years for river valley projects vs. 5 years for others — specific detail frequently tested
Mandatory studies: carrying capacity study, downstream flow assessment, fisheries impact, displacement and R&R plan
Cumulative impact controversy: Uttarakhand HC and NGT cases challenging multiple hydro projects on Ganga tributaries without CIA — led to moratorium on some projects
